title: Sum of Array Elements
prompt: Return the sum of all integers in an array.

steps: Initialize an accumulator to zero.
Iterate through each array element and add to accumulator.
Return the accumulator after the loop.
approach.example: Input [2,4,1], size 3 -> acc=0 -> acc=2 -> acc=6 -> acc=7 -> return 7.

walkthroughSteps: Function sets local variable total to 0.
Loop visits each index i and adds nums[i] to total.
After loop ends the function returns total containing the sum.
commonMistakes: Using uninitialized accumulator (not setting total = 0).
Loop bound off-by-one using i <= size instead of i < size.

title: Find Maximum Value
prompt: Return the largest integer in a non-empty array.

steps: Assume first element is maximum.
Traverse remaining elements comparing to current max.
Update max when a larger value is found and return it.
approach.example: Input [3,1,7,5] -> max=3 -> compare 1 keep 3 -> 7 updates max=7 -> 5 keep 7 -> return 7.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize maxVal with nums[0] so there's a valid baseline.
Loop from index 1 to size-1 comparing nums[i] to maxVal.
When nums[i] is larger assign it to maxVal; after loop return maxVal.
commonMistakes: Setting initial maxVal to 0 which fails for all-negative arrays.
Using i <= size causing out-of-bounds access.

title: Find Minimum Value
prompt: Return the smallest integer in a non-empty array.

steps: Set min to the first element.
Iterate through the array comparing each element to min.
Update min when a smaller element is found and return it.
approach.example: Input [6,2,9,2] -> min=6 -> 2 updates min=2 -> 9 keep 2 -> 2 keep 2 -> return 2.

walkthroughSteps: minVal initialized to nums[0] to handle any values.
Loop compares each nums[i] with minVal and updates when smaller.
Return minVal after scanning all elements.
commonMistakes: Using a large constant like INT_MAX without including limits header (missing include).
Forgetting to handle size==0; function assumes non-empty array.

title: Linear Search Index
prompt: Return the index of target in array or -1 if not found.

steps: Iterate through array indices from 0 to size-1.
Compare each element to target.
Return index on match; after loop return -1.
approach.example: Input [5,3,8], target 3 -> i=0 no -> i=1 match -> return 1.

walkthroughSteps: Loop checks each index i sequentially.
If nums[i] equals target the function returns i immediately.
If loop finishes without match the function returns -1 to signal not found.
commonMistakes: Returning 0 when not found instead of -1.
Using assignment (=) instead of equality (==) in the if condition.

title: Count Even Numbers
prompt: Count how many elements in an integer array are even.

steps: Initialize a counter to zero.
Loop through each element and check evenness with modulo.
Increment counter for even elements and return it.
approach.example: Input [2,7,4] -> count=0 -> 2 even count=1 -> 7 skip -> 4 even count=2 -> return 2.

walkthroughSteps: Start with count = 0 to accumulate evens.
Each loop iteration tests nums[i] % 2 == 0 and increments count when true.
Return the final count after scanning all elements.
commonMistakes: Using nums[i] / 2 == 0 instead of modulo for even check.
Forgetting to handle negative numbers — modulo still works but some beginners misinterpret sign.

title: Average of Array
prompt: Compute the integer average (floor) of array elements.

steps: Sum all elements using a larger accumulator if needed.
Divide the sum by size using integer division.
Return the quotient as the average.

walkthroughSteps: Use long sum to avoid overflow on many elements.
Accumulate each nums[i] into sum in the loop.
Compute integer division sum/size and return as int.
commonMistakes: Using int sum causing overflow for large arrays.
Dividing before summing or using float when integer average was requested.

title: Reverse Array In Place
prompt: Reverse the elements of an array in place.

steps: Use two pointers at start and end of array.
Swap elements at the two pointers.
Move pointers inward until they meet.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize left and right pointers to the ends of the array.
Swap nums[left] and nums[right] using a temporary variable.
Increment left and decrement right until left >= right; array is reversed.
commonMistakes: Using a swap that overwrites a value without a temporary variable.
Loop condition left <= right causing an unnecessary middle swap for odd sizes.

title: Rotate Right By One
prompt: Rotate array elements to the right by one position in place.

steps: Save the last element in a temporary variable.
Shift all elements one position to the right from end to start.
Place saved last element at index 0.
approach.example: Input [1,2,3] -> save 3 -> shift to [1,1,2] -> set index0=3 -> [3,1,2].

walkthroughSteps: Handle trivial sizes early to avoid work.
Store the last element before overwriting it.
Shift elements right and then write the stored last value to index 0.
commonMistakes: Loop direction wrong (left-to-right) causing overwrite of needed values.
Not handling size==0 or size==1 leading to unnecessary operations.

title: Count Vowels in String
prompt: Return the number of vowel characters in a null-terminated string (case-insensitive).

steps: Iterate characters until null terminator.
Convert letter to lowercase and check if it is a,e,i,o,u.
Increment counter for vowels and return it.
approach.example: Input "Hi!" -> 'H'->h not vowel -> 'i' vowel count=1 -> return 1.

walkthroughSteps: Loop reads each character until '\0' to avoid buffer overrun.
Uppercase letters are converted to lowercase for uniform checks.
Check membership in vowel set and increment count accordingly.
commonMistakes: Comparing characters to string literals like "a" instead of 'a'.
Forgetting to stop at the null terminator causing undefined behavior.

title: Check Palindrome String
prompt: Return 1 if a null-terminated string is a palindrome (letters only), else 0.

steps: Use two indices at start and end and skip non-letters.
Compare letters case-insensitively.
If all matched return 1, otherwise return 0.
approach.example: Input "A man, a plan" -> compare a vs n skip spaces -> eventually all match -> return 1.

walkthroughSteps: Compute right as index of last character before '\0'.
Advance left/right skipping non-letter characters to focus comparisons.
Normalize case and compare characters; mismatch returns 0, otherwise return 1 after loop.
commonMistakes: Not skipping non-letter characters leading to false negatives.
Using strlen in loop repeatedly causing extra cost (though still easy).

title: Remove First Occurrence
prompt: Remove the first occurrence of target from array by shifting and return new size.

steps: Find index of first target occurrence.
Shift subsequent elements left by one position.
Return original size minus one if removed, else original size.
approach.example: Input [4,2,3,2], target 2 -> remove index1 -> shift -> [4,3,2] -> return 3.

walkthroughSteps: Scan to find first index where nums[i]==target and record idx.
If not found return original size; otherwise shift elements left starting at idx.
Return size-1 to reflect removal.
commonMistakes: Shifting with wrong loop bounds causing last element duplication.
Returning idx instead of new size by mistake.

title: Sum of Two Smallest
prompt: Return the sum of the two smallest distinct elements in an array of at least two elements.

steps: Track smallest and second smallest while scanning once.
Update both when a new smaller value is found.
Return their sum after the loop.
approach.example: Input [5,1,3,1] -> min=5 sec=1 -> see 1 update min=1 sec=5 -> see 3 sec=3 -> see 1 equal skip -> return 1+3=4.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize min1 and min2 from first two elements and order them.
Iterate remaining elements updating min1/min2 appropriately.
After scan return the sum min1 + min2.
commonMistakes: Not ordering initial min1/min2 leading to wrong updates.
Assuming elements are distinct; this code allows equal values but beginners may mishandle ties.

title: Prefix Sum Array
prompt: Produce an output array of same size where each element is the prefix sum up to that index.

steps: Create running sum variable initialized to zero.
Iterate input and add current element to running sum.
Write running sum into output array at same index.
approach.example: Input [1,2,3] -> out[0]=1 -> out[1]=3 -> out[2]=6 -> return out.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize running to 0 to accumulate sums.
For each index add nums[i] to running and store into out[i].
After loop out contains prefix sums for every index.
commonMistakes: Writing to out before updating running causing off-by-one sums.
Using the same array for in-place without documenting behavior; this function expects separate out array.

title: Count Occurrences
prompt: Return how many times a target value appears in an array.

steps: Initialize counter to zero.
Loop through array and increment when element equals target.
Return the counter after scanning.

walkthroughSteps: Start with count = 0 to accumulate matches.
Each iteration compares nums[i] to target and increments count on match.
Return final count representing total occurrences.
commonMistakes: Using assignment in the if condition (nums[i] = target).
Forgetting to initialize count to zero.

title: Clamp Values In Range
prompt: Clamp each element of an array to lie within [low, high] modifying the array in place.

steps: Iterate through each element.
If element is less than low set it to low.
If element is greater than high set it to high; otherwise leave it.

walkthroughSteps: Loop visits each index and compares nums[i] to bounds.
Assign low when below bound or high when above bound.
In-place modification ensures no extra memory is used; function returns void.
commonMistakes: Using separate arrays unnecessarily increasing space.
Using incorrect comparison signs causing off-by-one clamping errors.

title: Sum of Positive Elements
prompt: Return the sum of all positive integers in an array.

steps: Initialize an accumulator to zero.
Iterate through each array element.
Add the element to the accumulator only if it is positive and return the accumulator.
approach.example: Input [-1,4,0,3] -> sum=0 -> add 4 -> sum=4 -> add 3 -> sum=7 -> return 7.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize sum to 0 to collect positive values.
Loop over indices 0..size-1 and test nums[i] > 0.
Add qualifying values to sum and return the final total.
commonMistakes: Using >= 0 instead of > 0 when zero should be excluded.
Forgetting to initialize sum leading to undefined behavior.

title: Product of Array Elements
prompt: Return the product of all integers in an array.

steps: Set a product variable to 1.
Multiply the product by each element while iterating.
Return the product after processing all elements.
approach.example: Input [2,3,4] -> prod=1 -> prod=2 -> prod=6 -> prod=24 -> return 24.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize prod to 1 as the multiplicative identity.
Iterate through the array multiplying prod by nums[i].
Return prod which holds the cumulative product.
commonMistakes: Initializing prod to 0 which yields zero result.
Not using a larger type (long) when product may overflow int.

title: All Elements Equal
prompt: Return 1 if all elements in the array are equal, otherwise return 0.

steps: If size is 0 or 1 return 1.
Store the first element as a reference value.
Compare each subsequent element to the reference and return 0 on first mismatch.
approach.example: Input [5,5,5] -> ref=5 -> all comparisons equal -> return 1.

walkthroughSteps: Handle trivial arrays by returning 1 for size 0 or 1.
Use nums[0] as the reference value for comparisons.
Return 0 immediately on first mismatch; otherwise return 1 after the loop.
commonMistakes: Returning 0 for empty array incorrectly; empty array should be considered all equal here.
Comparing with wrong index bounds causing out-of-range access.

title: Check Sorted Nondecreasing
prompt: Return 1 if the array is sorted in nondecreasing order, otherwise return 0.

steps: Traverse the array from index 1 to size-1.
Compare each element with the previous element.
If any element is less than the previous return 0; otherwise return 1.

walkthroughSteps: Loop from the second element comparing nums[i] with nums[i-1].
If any pair violates nondecreasing order return 0 immediately.
If loop completes without violation return 1.
commonMistakes: Starting loop at i=0 and accessing nums[-1].
Using wrong comparison sign causing inverted logic.

title: Second Largest Distinct Value
prompt: Return the second largest distinct value in an array; assume at least two distinct values exist.

steps: Initialize max1 and max2 from the first two elements and order them.
Scan remaining elements updating max1 and max2 when appropriate.
Return max2 after scanning all elements.

walkthroughSteps: Order the first two elements so max1 >= max2 to start.
For each new element, if it's greater than max1 shift max1 to max2 and set max1.
If it's between max2 and max1 update max2; return max2 at the end.
commonMistakes: Not handling equal values correctly leading to duplicate max1/max2.
Assuming array length exactly two without validating distinctness.

title: Swap Adjacent Pairs
prompt: Swap every pair of adjacent elements in the array in place.

steps: Iterate over the array with step size 2.
For each pair swap the two elements using a temporary variable.
If the array length is odd leave the final element unchanged.

walkthroughSteps: Loop with i incremented by 2 to visit each adjacent pair.
Swap nums[i] and nums[i+1] using a temporary variable.
If size is odd the last element remains unchanged.
commonMistakes: Using i++ instead of i+=2 causing overlapping swaps.
Forgetting to check i+1 < size leading to out-of-bounds access.

title: Move Zeros To End
prompt: Move all zeros in the array to the end while preserving the order of non-zero elements.

steps: Use a write index to place non-zero elements sequentially.
Copy each non-zero element to the write position and increment write.
After copying, fill remaining positions with zeros.

walkthroughSteps: Maintain write pointer where the next non-zero should be placed.
Copy each non-zero nums[i] to nums[write] and increment write.
After loop fill remaining indices with zeros to move zeros to the end.
commonMistakes: Swapping zeros and non-zeros instead of copying causing order changes.
Using an extra array unnecessarily increasing space.

title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
prompt: Merge two sorted arrays into a single sorted output array; both inputs are sorted ascending.

steps: Use three indices for the two inputs and the output.
Compare current elements from both inputs and copy the smaller to output.
After one input is exhausted copy remaining elements from the other input.

walkthroughSteps: Maintain pointers i and j for inputs and k for output position.
Compare a[i] and b[j], copy the smaller to out and advance pointers.
After one input is exhausted copy the remainder from the other array.
commonMistakes: Overrunning output if its size isn't na+nb; caller must provide correct out size.
Using < instead of <= causing unstable ordering for equal elements.

title: Remove Duplicates From Sorted Array
prompt: Remove duplicates from a sorted array in place and return the new length.

steps: Return 0 immediately for empty input.
Use a write pointer to store the next unique element.
Copy current element when it differs from the last unique and return write as the new length.

walkthroughSteps: Handle empty array by returning 0.
Use write pointer to keep the next position for a unique value.
Compare nums[i] to nums[write-1] and copy when different; return write at the end.
commonMistakes: Comparing nums[i] to nums[i-1] instead of nums[write-1] causing logic errors.
Returning size instead of write when duplicates exist.

title: Index of Minimum Element
prompt: Return the index of the minimum element in the array.

steps: Assume index 0 is the minimum index.
Traverse the array comparing elements to the current minimum index.
Update the minimum index when a smaller element is found and return it.
approach.example: Input [7,2,5] -> minIdx=0 -> see 2 update to 1 -> return 1.

walkthroughSteps: Initialize minIdx to 0 to have a baseline index.
Loop through remaining indices comparing nums[i] to nums[minIdx].
Update minIdx on smaller values and return it after the loop.
commonMistakes: Returning the value instead of the index by mistake.
Not handling empty array; function assumes size >= 1.

title: Count Negative Numbers
prompt: Return the count of negative numbers in an integer array.

steps: Initialize a counter to zero.
Iterate through each element and increment the counter when the element is negative.
Return the counter after scanning the array.
approach.example: Input [-2,0,3,-1] -> count increments for -2 and -1 -> return 2.

walkthroughSteps: Start count at 0 to accumulate negatives.
Check nums[i] < 0 for each element and increment count on match.
Return the final count after the loop completes.
commonMistakes: Using <= 0 instead of < 0 when zero should not be counted.
Forgetting to initialize count leading to garbage value.

title: Reverse String In Place
prompt: Reverse a null-terminated string in place.

steps: Find the string length by scanning to the null terminator.
Use two indices at the ends and swap characters inward.
Stop when indices meet or cross and leave the null terminator.

walkthroughSteps: Compute right as the index of the last character before '\0'.
Swap characters at left and right using a temporary variable.
Advance pointers until left >= right; string is reversed in place.
commonMistakes: Using strlen repeatedly inside the loop causing extra cost.
Not handling empty string where right becomes -1; loop condition prevents swaps.

title: Anagram Check Letters Only
prompt: Return 1 if two null-terminated strings are anagrams considering letters only and case-insensitive, otherwise return 0.

steps: Count letter frequencies for the first string normalized to lowercase.
Subtract frequencies using letters from the second string.
If all frequency counts are zero the strings are anagrams; otherwise return 0.

walkthroughSteps: Normalize letters to lowercase and count frequencies from the first string.
Subtract counts using letters from the second string.
If any frequency is non-zero after both passes return 0; otherwise return 1.
commonMistakes: Including non-letter characters in counts causing false negatives.
Failing to normalize case leading to mismatches.

title: Count Consonants
prompt: Return the number of consonant letters in a null-terminated string (case-insensitive).

steps: Iterate characters until the null terminator.
Normalize letters to lowercase and check if alphabetic.
If alphabetic and not a vowel increment counter.
Return the counter.

walkthroughSteps: Loop until '\0' to process each character safely.
Normalize uppercase letters to lowercase for uniform checks.
Test alphabetic range and exclude vowels; increment count for consonants and return it.
commonMistakes: Checking vowels before normalizing case causing missed matches.
Using string functions like strlen inside the loop causing extra cost.

title: Check Prime
prompt: Return 1 if a positive integer n is prime, otherwise return 0 (n >= 1).

steps: Handle n <= 1 and small base cases.
Test divisors from 2 up to sqrt(n).
Return 0 on first divisor found; otherwise return 1.

walkthroughSteps: Reject n <= 1 and accept small primes 2 and 3 quickly.
Eliminate even numbers early to skip half the checks.
Loop odd divisors up to sqrt(n); a found divisor returns 0, otherwise return 1.
commonMistakes: Looping up to n-1 instead of sqrt(n) causing unnecessary work.
Not handling n==2 correctly when checking evenness.

title: GCD of Array
prompt: Return the greatest common divisor (GCD) of all positive integers in an array (size >= 1).

steps: Implement helper to compute gcd of two numbers using Euclid's algorithm.
Initialize result with first element.
Iterate remaining elements updating result = gcd(result, nums[i]).
Return final gcd.

walkthroughSteps: gcd2 uses Euclid's loop to reduce b until zero and returns absolute a.
gcdArray starts with nums[0] and folds gcd across the array.
Each step reduces the result; final value is gcd of all elements.
commonMistakes: Using recursive gcd without base case causing stack issues for large inputs.
Not taking absolute values leading to negative gcd for negative inputs.

title: Prefix Maximums
prompt: Fill an output array where out[i] is the maximum of nums[0..i].

steps: Initialize running maximum with first element.
Iterate array updating running maximum.
Assign running maximum to out[i] at each step.

walkthroughSteps: Handle empty input by returning early.
Maintain cur as the running maximum and update when a larger element appears.
Write cur into out[i] each iteration so out holds prefix maximums.
commonMistakes: Writing out[i] before updating cur causing off-by-one results.
Assuming out is pre-initialized instead of assigning every index.

title: Remove At Index
prompt: Remove the element at a given index by shifting subsequent elements left and return the new size; if index invalid return original size.

steps: Validate index is within 0..size-1.
Shift elements left starting from index to size-2.
Return size-1 when removal occurs, else return original size.

walkthroughSteps: Check index bounds to avoid out-of-range access.
Shift each element left from the removal index to overwrite the removed slot.
Return the decremented size to reflect the removal.
commonMistakes: Using i <= size - 1 in loop causing unnecessary copy of last element.
Returning index instead of new size by mistake.

title: Insert At Index
prompt: Insert a value at a given index by shifting elements right; assume capacity >= size+1 and return new size; if index invalid return original size.

steps: Validate index between 0 and size inclusive.
Shift elements right from end to index to make space.
Assign value at index and return size+1.

walkthroughSteps: Validate index and capacity to ensure safe insertion.
Shift elements right starting from size down to index to open a slot.
Place val at index and return the increased size.
commonMistakes: Shifting left-to-right causing overwrite instead of right-to-left.
Not checking capacity leading to buffer overflow.

title: Sum of Odd Elements
prompt: Return the sum of all odd integers in an array.

steps: Initialize sum to zero.
Iterate through array and test oddness with modulo.
Add odd elements to sum and return it.

walkthroughSteps: Start sum at 0 to accumulate odd values.
Check nums[i] % 2 != 0 to detect odd numbers.
Add odd values to sum and return the final total.
commonMistakes: Using nums[i] % 2 == 1 which fails for negative odd numbers; use != 0.
Forgetting to initialize sum leading to undefined behavior.

title: Last Index Of
prompt: Return the last index where target appears in array or -1 if not found.

steps: Iterate from end of array toward start.
Compare each element to target.
Return index on first match; if none found return -1.
approach.example: Input [1,2,3,2], target 2 -> check from end -> match at 3 -> return 3.

walkthroughSteps: Start loop at size-1 to search from the end.
Return immediately when nums[i] equals target to give last occurrence.
If loop finishes without match return -1.
commonMistakes: Looping forward and overwriting index variable instead of returning last match.
Using unsigned index type causing infinite loop when i becomes negative.

title: Check Strictly Decreasing
prompt: Return 1 if array elements are strictly decreasing (each element < previous), else 0.

steps: Traverse array from index 1 to end.
Compare current element with previous; if not strictly less return 0.
If all checks pass return 1.

walkthroughSteps: Loop from second element comparing nums[i] with nums[i-1].
If any nums[i] is not less than previous return 0 immediately.
If loop completes return 1 indicating strict decrease.
commonMistakes: Using <= instead of < when strictness is required.
Starting loop at i=0 and accessing nums[-1].

title: Count Above Average
prompt: Return the number of elements strictly greater than the integer average of the array.

steps: Compute integer average by summing elements and dividing by size.
Iterate again counting elements greater than average.
Return the count.
approach.example: Input [1,2,3,4] -> avg=2 -> elements >2 are 3 and 4 -> return 2.

walkthroughSteps: Sum elements in a long to avoid overflow and compute integer average.
Loop again to compare each element to avg and increment count when greater.
Return the count of elements strictly above the average.
commonMistakes: Using float average when integer average was requested.
Dividing before summing or using int sum causing overflow on large inputs.

title: Pair Sum Exists Brute Force
prompt: Return 1 if any two distinct elements in the array sum to target, otherwise return 0 (O(n^2) solution).

steps: Use two nested loops to test every pair of indices i<j.
If nums[i]+nums[j]==target return 1 immediately.
If no pair found return 0.

walkthroughSteps: Outer loop picks first element and inner loop checks all later elements.
Return 1 immediately when a matching pair is found.
If loops finish without match return 0.
commonMistakes: Checking pairs with i==j allowing same element twice.
Breaking only inner loop on match instead of returning causing incorrect result.

title: Replace With Neighbor Product
prompt: Replace each element with the product of its immediate neighbors; keep first and last elements unchanged.

steps: If size < 3 nothing changes; return.
Use a temporary array to store new values for middle elements.
Copy temporary values back into original array.

walkthroughSteps: Handle small arrays early where no middle elements exist.
Compute products for middle indices into a temporary array to avoid overwriting neighbors.
Copy temporary results back to nums so first and last remain original and middles are replaced.
commonMistakes: Overwriting nums in-place while computing causing wrong neighbor values.
Forgetting to preserve first and last elements.
